title: English for Work
subtitle: Professional track
description: The English of meetings, emails and interviews — professional situations, practised out loud. A track that runs alongside Foundations.

themes.title: Monday stand-up
themes.subtitle: Report your week
themes.situation: You report progress in a stand-up: what you did, what you're doing, what's blocked.

themes.title: The interview rehearsal
themes.subtitle: Sell your experience
themes.situation: A job interview rehearsal: present yourself, describe projects and answer the hard questions.

lessons.title: In meetings
lessons.goal: Report progress, ask for clarification and disagree politely in a meeting.

explanation: Structure beats improvisation: “Last week I finished X. This week I'm working on Y. I'm blocked on Z.”
Clarify before you guess: “Sorry, could you clarify that?” “Just to make sure I understand…”
Disagree with data, not people: “I see it slightly differently — the numbers show…”

examples.text: Last week I finished the report.
This week I'm working on the budget.
Just to make sure I understand: we ship on Friday?
I see it slightly differently — the data shows a drop.

expressions.text: Just to make sure I understand, …

lessons.situation: Monday stand-up: report what you finished, what you're on and what's blocked; clarify one point and politely disagree with a plan once.

questions.prompt: Report one thing you finished last week.
expected: Last week I finished <task>.
questions.watch: “Last week I finish” — done work takes past simple.

questions.prompt: Report what you're doing this week.
expected: This week I'm working on <task>.
questions.watch: “This week I work on” sounds like a routine — use the continuous.

questions.prompt: Tell the team what is blocking you. (approvals)
expected: I'm blocked on the approvals.
questions.watch: “I'm blocked by the approvals” also works; “I block on” doesn't.

questions.prompt: Ask for clarification about the deadline.
expected: Sorry, could you clarify the deadline?
Could you clarify when the deadline is?
questions.watch: Clarify + the thing: the deadline, the owner, the scope.

questions.prompt: Confirm a decision you half-heard. (ship on Friday)
expected: Just to make sure I understand: we ship on Friday?
questions.watch: Repeat the decision back as a question.

questions.prompt: Disagree with a plan, politely, with data.
expected: I see it slightly differently — the data shows a drop.
I see your point; however, the numbers say otherwise.
questions.watch: Data first, tone soft: no “you're wrong”.

exercises.explain: Last week + past simple for completed work.

exercises.prompt: This week I'm ___ on the budget. (work)
Say what blocks you: the client's approval.
answers: i'm blocked on the client's approval
i am blocked on the approval
i'm blocked by the client's approval

lessons.title: Professional emails
lessons.goal: Write short professional emails: request, confirm and follow up.

explanation: Email skeleton: greeting → purpose in line one → details → clear ask → sign-off. “Hi Marta, I'm writing about… Could you…? Thanks, Dan.”
Requests: “Could you send… by Wednesday?” Deadlines make asks actionable. Follow-ups stay light: “Just following up on my email below.”
Register: no contractions is safer in formal mail; “I would be grateful if…” is the formal ask.

examples.text: Could you send the figures by Wednesday?
Just following up on my email below.
I would be grateful if you could confirm.

expressions.text: I'm writing about / to ask about …
expressions.note: No weather talk in work mail.

expressions.text: I would be grateful if you could …

lessons.situation: You need numbers from a busy colleague: write the request, set a deadline, and then follow up two days later — politely.

questions.prompt: Open an email about the quarterly figures.
expected: I'm writing about the quarterly figures.
questions.watch: Line one states the topic — no “I hope you are well” padding needed.

questions.prompt: Ask for the figures with a deadline. (Wednesday)
expected: Could you send the figures by Wednesday?
questions.watch: by + day: “until Wednesday” is different — by is the limit.

questions.prompt: Point to the report you attached.
expected: Please find the report attached.
questions.watch: The fixed phrase is find … attached.

questions.prompt: Follow up on an unanswered email, lightly.
expected: Just following up on my email below.
questions.watch: “Why didn't you answer?” is never the opening.

questions.prompt: Make the formal version of the ask. (confirm attendance)
expected: I would be grateful if you could confirm your attendance.
questions.watch: would be grateful + if you could.

questions.prompt: Choose a safe sign-off for a client.
expected: Best regards.
Kind regards.
questions.watch: Cheers and hugs stay with friends.

exercises.explain: by Friday = not later than Friday.

answers: i would be grateful if you could confirm your attendance
i would be grateful if you could confirm attendance
exercises.explain: I would be grateful if you could…

lessons.title: Job interviews
lessons.goal: Present yourself, describe achievements and handle hard questions in an interview.

explanation: The achievement formula: situation → action → result. “The team was behind (S). I rebuilt the schedule (A) and we shipped on time (R).”
Weakness questions want honesty plus growth: “I used to over-plan; now I timebox decisions.”
Buy time politely: “That's a good question — let me think for a second.” Silence feels longer to you than to them.

examples.text: I've led a team of five for three years.
The project was behind, so I rebuilt the schedule.
As a result, we shipped two weeks early.
examples.meaning: Result with a number if possible.

examples.text: I used to over-plan; now I timebox decisions.
That's a good question — let me think for a second.
I'm particularly proud of the migration project.

expressions.text: Let me think for a second.

lessons.situation: Interview rehearsal: introduce your experience, tell one achievement with S-A-R, answer the weakness question and negotiate next steps.

questions.prompt: Describe your current role and how long you've had it.
expected: I've worked as a <role> for <time>.
I've been a <role> since <year>.

questions.prompt: Tell one achievement as a story. (situation → action → result)
expected: The project was behind, so I rebuilt the schedule, and as a result we shipped on time.
questions.watch: The result is the point — land it with as a result.

questions.prompt: Answer the weakness question honestly with growth.
expected: I used to over-plan; now I timebox decisions.
questions.watch: used to for the old habit, now for the fix.

questions.prompt: Buy time on a hard question.
expected: That's a good question — let me think for a second.
questions.watch: Then structure the answer: point, example, close.

questions.prompt: Explain why you want this job. (growth + contribution)
expected: I want to grow into <area>, and I believe I can contribute <strength>.
questions.watch: What you gain AND what you bring.

expected: Thank you — I look forward to hearing from you.

exercises.explain: since + point in time; for + period.

exercises.prompt: ___ a result, we shipped two weeks early.

answers: That's a good question let me think for a second
i used to over-plan now i timebox decisions
i used to over plan now i timebox decisions
